template.title: Vignette Expansion

elements.label: Identify the Vignette Core
elements.description: Define the one-sentence premise, emotional energy, and exposed aspect of world or self.
elements.goal: Pinpoint the emotional or conceptual nucleus of the vignette.
actions: Summarize the vignette in one sentence: “This is a moment where ___ realizes/feels/confronts ___.”
Identify the emotional energy or thematic tension that drives it (e.g. longing, loss, curiosity, defiance).
Decide what aspect of the world or self this vignette exposes.
elements.output: 1–2 sentences defining the vignette’s core premise and emotional axis.

elements.label: Situate It Within the Modular Spine
elements.description: Place the vignette in a module role and identify possible connections.
elements.goal: Place the vignette in the interlocking modular network.
actions: Decide which module the vignette belongs to (or could become).
Identify 1–2 other modules it could connect to through theme, motif, or character continuity.
elements.output: A labeled position for the vignette (e.g. “Expansion module, linked to Origin via emotional inversion”).

elements.label: Define the Modular Links
elements.description: Describe connective concepts, objects, echoes, inversions, and link type.
elements.goal: Create the connective tissue that allows the vignette to interlock with others.
actions: For each chosen link, write a short bridge note.
Identify the concept, object, or emotional echo connecting the modules.
Describe how tone or imagery might recur or invert.
Mark each link as direct (narrative) or resonant (thematic/metaphoric).
elements.output: A small diagram or list of 2–4 link notes.

elements.label: Expand the Internal Architecture
elements.description: Develop initiation, distortion, and reverberation micro-stages.
elements.goal: Evolve the vignette from a single event into a multi-phase module with internal rhythm.
actions: Break the vignette into three micro-stages: Initiation (the moment begins or the threshold is crossed); Distortion (the premise destabilizes; perception or tone shifts); Reverberation (a change in understanding or mood settles).
Layer sensory or conceptual motifs across these micro-stages for cohesion.
elements.output: 3 short paragraph sketches or beat outlines.

elements.label: Integrate the Meta-Layer
elements.description: Identify a principle and describe its system-level role across modules.
elements.goal: Give the module participation in the story’s systemic logic (its modular engine).
actions: Identify what principle this vignette expresses (e.g. entropy, recursion, emergence, memory).
Draft one or two system-level statements about how this principle plays out across modules.
elements.output: A few sentences defining its role in the modular ecology.

elements.label: Expand Outward (Iteration)
elements.description: Extract recurring elements and draft alternate perspectives, media, times, or tones.
elements.goal: Turn the vignette’s core into a generative seed for other modules.
actions: Extract 1–3 elements (object, phrase, emotional pivot) that can recur in other modules.
Write alternate interpretations or versions of the vignette (different perspective, medium, time, or emotional tone).
Place each variation in another module slot to form crosslinks.
elements.output: Draft notes for 2–3 derived fragments or echoes.

elements.label: Assemble and Calibrate
elements.description: Place the vignette in a sequence or lattice according to thematic resonance, then test rhythm and density.
elements.goal: Integrate the expanded vignette into the larger network.
actions: Place it in sequence or lattice according to thematic resonance, not chronology.
Test modular rhythm: initiation → reflection → divergence → convergence → afterimage.
Adjust tone and density to maintain equilibrium across modules.
elements.output: A working version of the vignette as a complete modular node, ready to link into the full structure.

elements.label: Optional: Meta Weaving Layer
elements.description: Define recursion, callbacks, inversions, loops, and reading-order effects when applicable.
elements.goal: Add recursion and reader-agency structure when the modular story uses them.
actions: Define how this vignette could reactivate earlier nodes (callbacks, inversions, loops).
Define how its meaning changes depending on reading order or context.
elements.output: An optional specification of recursion, callbacks, inversions, loops, and reading-order effects.

source_structures.modular_spine_model: Interlocking segments forming a dynamic network, not a linear story.

template.interpretation_guard: Workflow order is not fictional-world chronology. Module slots are functional positions, not a mandatory linear sequence. Direct and resonant links remain distinct.
